subject: Token-tier smoothing & hurdle breakpoint proposal

Subject: Token-tier smoothing & hurdle breakpoint proposal

Samir —

Thanks again for taking time yesterday. Per our conversation, I attached a starter ladder that balances headline discounts with a smoothing mechanism to avoid a single large cliff between tiers. Key design goals I used:

- Keep effective blended rate predictable for you across a 12-month ramp.
- Give a visible incentive to cross meaningful throughput hurdles without a one-off step-function drop in price.
- Preserve marginal pricing for burst usage to avoid surprises on month-to-month invoicing.

High-level (see spreadsheet):
- Baseline (0-250M tokens/mo): $0.00110/token
- Hurdle band A (250M-750M): marginal price $0.00095 (blended effective ~ $0.00102 if evenly distributed)
- Hurdle band B (750M-2B): marginal price $0.00075 (blended effective ~ $0.00086)
- Smoothing window: 2-month graceful step where crossing a breakpoint triggers a prorated blended credit to avoid abrupt jump in your effective monthly rate.

Practical notes: the smoothing is an operational credit we apply on invoices (not a change to runtime routing). We can pilot this for three months and include a true-up at quarter end. Also included two optional constraints in the sheet: a minimum monthly committed floor and a velocity credit to accelerate discounts if you consistently grow month-over-month.

Ask: can you confirm whether procurement needs a minimum-guarantee clause, or if a purely usage-based commit (with a soft monthly floor) is acceptable? I copied Karthik for pricing operations and Naomi for contract/terms.

Attachments: acme_token_ladder_v1.xlsx (breakdown + sample invoice), acme_terms_redline.pdf (paperwork with redlines)

3) We anticipate a fast POC for launch (2–3 months) that could see spiky usage. Can you confirm that spikes in a single day won't retroactively change the rate for the whole month (i.e., marginal billing per token)?

Samir / Marcus —

Quick answers from ops/pricing:

1) Smoothing credit mechanics: we modeled it two ways in the sheet — (A) percentage-of-delta credit applied pro-rata for the month you cross the breakpoint; (B) token-credit equivalent for the delta. We typically recommend the % approach (A) because it keeps invoices simple and aligns with blended effective rate targets. The attached version defaults to approach (A).

2) Velocity credit stacking: velocity (growth) credits are additive but capped. So you could receive a hurdle discount + a velocity bonus up to an aggregate cap (e.g., up to 18% total off baseline). We do that to prevent double-dipping while still rewarding sustained growth.

3) Spiky POC behavior: billing is strictly marginal per token. We will not retroactively rebucket earlier tokens in the month except for the smoothing credit construct — that is intentionally a forward-adjusting credit applied when the threshold is crossed. In other words: spikes can push you into a lower marginal price for tokens after the breakpoint; spikes themselves don't cause retroactive billing for tokens already invoiced without the smoothing credit (the smoothing credit smooths month-to-month impact).

Operational note: for the 2-month pilot smoothing, we need your team to agree to a monthly reporting webhook so we can detect crossing events and apply credits automatically. Naomi — can you jump in on the T&Cs side?

—Karthik

Hi Samir —

From the contract side, high-level comments on the redline PDF:

- Minimum guarantee: we can support a soft minimum (month-to-month floor with true-up at quarter end). Hard annual minimums introduce revenue recognition and billing complexities for pilots, so we avoid them for pilot / POC phases.
- Smoothing credit: we can describe it as an invoice-level credit triggered by crossing events and capped to a specific % per month (e.g., max 10% of the invoice). That gives both sides predictability.
- Audit / usage reporting: recommend adding a clause for webhook + monthly CSV export to reconcile spikes.
- Cancellation & overage: define a 30-day notice for downgrade of committed bands; overage margin will be billed at baseline rate unless agreed otherwise.

Action items for Acme legal: please mark up the attached PDF and call out any non-negotiables (e.g., hard annual minima or audit window requests). Once we get that back, we can produce a final pilot SOW.

Regards,

Team —

Thanks for the quick clarifications. High-level feedback from Acme:

- Procurement is comfortable with a soft monthly floor and quarter true-up — they will not accept an unconditional annual commitment for a POC.
- They asked that smoothing credits be capped and fully visible line-items on the invoice (good with your percent-of-delta proposal).
- Legal (Gina) will send a redline by end of week; expect items around data residency and the audit clause.
- Two asks from engineering: 1) a short-run opt-out if the integration causes instability for their traffic (we suggested a 14-day rollback window), and 2) the webhook endpoint details so they can implement the reporting.

Next steps: I'll share the procurement redline once Gina finishes it. If all looks good, can Redwood prepare a 3-month pilot SOW with a capped smoothing credit (10% max per month) and the velocity cap you suggested?
